implemented_capabilities.capability: Weighted step-free shortest-path routing in FalkorDB over line/platform/street nodes
implemented_capabilities.notes: Seeds Station/Access nodes and RIDE / STEP_FREE_TRANSFER edges with minute weights, then calls CALL algo.SPpaths({relTypes:['RIDE','STEP_FREE_TRANSFER'], weightProp:'minutes', pathCount:1}) via roQuery and converts the path into ride/transfer legs.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Disruption scenario graphs (copy the base graph and re-type affected edges to UNAVAILABLE_TRANSFER)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Uses GRAPH.COPY into a hash-named graph, then CREATE new UNAVAILABLE_TRANSFER edge + DELETE old STEP_FREE_TRANSFER for ids in $ids, so the same routing query reroutes with no code change; base graph untouched; scenarios memoised per outage set.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Dependency invalidation: derive which transfers fail when a lift is out, via BFS over TfL topology areas
implemented_capabilities.notes: Pure TypeScript BFS over area edges skipping unavailable lifts; a transfer is available only if every from/to area pair still has a path. Computed outside FalkorDB, then applied to the graph copy.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Live TfL lift disruption feed with 60 s cache
implemented_capabilities.notes: Fetches api.tfl.gov.uk Disruptions/Lifts/v2 with 10 s timeout, filters to lifts present in the 7-station network, stamps fetchedAt.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Network data build from official TfL station topology and timetables
implemented_capabilities.notes: Downloads the TfL detailed topology zip and derives requiredLifts and the demo outage lift rather than guessing, but the network is a hard-coded 7-station / 3-line subset and transfer times use fixed pace constants and a 1.3 corridor factor.

implemented_capabilities.capability: REST API and Live Mode locator
implemented_capabilities.notes: POST /api/route, /api/live/status (POST to keep coordinates out of URLs), GET /api/network, /api/health; demo mode toggles a simulated Green Park Lift 2 outage.

graph_models_and_cypher: Nodes: Station {id,name,naptanId,lat,lon,stepFreeStreetAccess}, Access {id,stationId,kind: street|line,line} with (Access)-[:AT]->(Station). Edges: RIDE {line,minutes}, STEP_FREE_TRANSFER {id,kind: entrance|interchange,minutes,liftsUsed,requiredLifts}, UNAVAILABLE_TRANSFER (same props, scenario graphs only). Cypher: UNWIND batch CREATE, CREATE INDEX on Access.id, GRAPH.COPY (db.selectGraph().copy), edge re-type via CREATE+DELETE, CALL algo.SPpaths with relTypes parameter and weightProp, roQuery for reads. Parameters are passed via params; relTypes is a bound param. FalkorDB-native, no APOC/GDS.
algorithms: algo.SPpaths weighted shortest path restricted to RIDE and STEP_FREE_TRANSFER (backend/src/graph/routing.ts:route)
BFS over area graph skipping failed lifts to decide transfer availability (backend/src/network/stepfree.ts:stepFreePath)
Scenario graph copy + edge retyping for what-if rerouting (backend/src/graph/routing.ts:createScenario)
Nearest-station haversine style lookup and London bounding check (backend/src/network/geo.ts)
frontend_interfaces: React PWA: LondonMap.tsx, TransitMap.tsx (schematic map), RoutePanel.tsx, Intro.tsx, About/InstallGuide pages, useStepFree hook, map layout/geo helpers
tests_present: Backend vitest: routing.test.ts (5, live FalkorDB), topology.test.ts (4, pure), api.test.ts (9, supertest); frontend vitest: describe/geo/layout tests (10). About 28 tests; routing and API tests need a FalkorDB at FALKORDB_URL. Not executed by auditor.
security_findings: backend/src/app.ts:25 - CORS origin falls back to true (any origin) when corsOrigin is not supplied; config.ts defaults to http://localhost:5173 so only exposed if constructed without it

backend/src/app.ts:32-80 - no authentication or rate limiting on routing endpoints; each distinct live outage set creates a new copied graph (backend/src/graph/routing.ts:createScenario) with no eviction, a slow resource-growth risk
backend/src/tfl/liftDisruptions.ts:35 - TfL app_key sent as URL query parameter (encodeURIComponent applied), may appear in logs; outbound call goes only to a constant api.tfl.gov.uk URL
backend/src/graph/routing.ts:~66-70 - seed() deletes every graph named <prefix> or <prefix>:* on start-up (scoped by prefix, intended)
No string-concatenated Cypher with user input found; no eval/exec; no hard-coded secrets (.env.example is empty)
duplicates_or_overlaps: Weighted routing with disruption rerouting overlaps other accessibility / mobility routing and 'what-if outage' scenario repos (e.g., other pathfinding and supply-route reroute demos); the copy-graph-and-retype pattern overlaps counterfactual / simulation approaches.
evidence_drift_relevance: MEDIUM - requiredLifts and the area-graph BFS implement dependency invalidation (a failed upstream lift invalidates dependent transfers and triggers re-derivation on a copied graph), with a fetchedAt-stamped live feed, but there is no provenance chain, supersession or approval gating.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: A compact, tested what-if pattern for FalkorDB: derive the set of invalidated edges outside the DB, GRAPH.COPY the base graph, retype the invalid edges, and rerun the same weighted algo.SPpaths query; directly reusable for counterfactual 'if this evidence/dependency is invalid, what else changes' views in Kairos.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB server (GRAPH.COPY, algo.SPpaths); TypeScript code must be re-implemented in Python (about 150 lines of logic)

strategy_rationale: Small, correct and FalkorDB-native, but TypeScript and tied to a 7-station TfL dataset; best taken as a Mobility & Accessibility pack plus a reusable scenario-copy pattern, re-implemented in Python rather than merged.
